note: Catalog-ish segment data from a targeted research pass (2026-09). Values are typical of Hytrol / Interroll / Monk / BestConnect catalog pages but have NOT each been confirmed against a specific catalog page -- treat as 'catalog-ish' until verified. Edit here, never in code.
sources: Hytrol tapered roller gravity curves (condrives.com) -- 30/45/60/90 deg
packagingconveyor.com + Remcon incline guides -- nose-over, angle rules of thumb
Monk roller conveyor technical spec PDF -- 600-3000 mm straights in 150 mm steps

curve.note: Catalogs quote INSIDE radius; centerline radius = inside + width/2. Gravity curves use tapered rollers (not modeled).

rules_of_thumb.note: Plain belt up to ~18-20 deg, totes <= 15 deg; test the worst SKU.

incline.note: Flat<->incline transitions use a nose-over (single up to ~15 deg, double for ~30 deg). Modeled as a vertical arc of nose_over_radius, inserted as extra length between the two segments rather than carved out of them.

RAT.label: Right-Angle Transfer
RAT.note: Powered transfer head; product moves sideways without turning.

MERGE.label: Merge Junction
MERGE.note: Auto-inserted where one line's end meets another line's body.

DIVERTER.label: Diverter / Sorter
DIVERTER.note: Outbound twin of a merge: goods leave the main line onto a docked branch.

BUFFER.label: Buffer / Accumulation
BUFFER.note: Accumulation zone: goods queue up against its end (zero-pressure buffer for a picker or a downstream stop).

LIFT.label: Vertical conveyor (S / C)
LIFT.note: Continuous vertical conveyor (S- / C-conveyor): the goods stay level on forks while the column carries them up. S carries on in the same direction (through a mezzanine), C comes back out above the entry.

ARB.label: Angled-roller align / turn
ARB.note: Angled-roller belt element: centres / aligns goods, or turns them 90 deg in motion (or a cheap fixed pivot for the turn).

WRAPPER.label: Pallet wrapper
WRAPPER.note: Conveyorised turntable stretch wrapper: the pallet rides onto the turntable, is wrapped (or unwrapped) and conveyed on. Scaled to the line's width.
